business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state company register distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (predominantly Civil Law, with French Commercial Code, Monetary and Financial Code and Finance Ministry general regulations; EU directives have direct and indirect effect)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-Mauritius DTA (as amended by the 2010 Protocol, in force as of 1 January 2014)
France-Holger? (placeholder) — corrected: France-Germany DTA (in force since 1 December 1959, as amended by the 2006/2008 amending protocols)
France-China DTA (in force since 1 January 2013, as amended by the 2013 Protocol)
France-United States DTA (signed, limited scope; the US-France BIT expired in 2022 but the DTA remains in force)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)
EU-Vietnam Investment Protection Agreement (in force since 1 August 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF), Articles L561-1 to L561-59 and D561-1 onward; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L123-7 and R123-45 to R123-51; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Law Sapin II); Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Regulation (EU) 2015/847; ACPR General Regulation; TRACFIN reporting under CMF L561-15.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted to judicial authorities, ACPR, French Treasury, TRACFIN, the commercial registry and statutory obligor institutions under AML/CFT law; no open public access to the beneficial owner register, consistent with the CJEU judgment in C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract of the foreign register of the direct shareholder and the ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the jurisdiction of the shareholder (e.g., Companies House, Delaware, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing state is party to the 1961 Apostille Convention); otherwise Consular Legalization by the French Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by all shareholders and the SAS President, including authority to file incorporation documents with the Guichet Unique and the Commercial Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization (depending on the notary's jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity card copies of the SAS President and each beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originals certified by a public notary or by the issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization when notarization is required; otherwise verified by registered legal counsel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate extraction of the shareholder's register evidencing the 25% ownership chain and the underlying UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder’s corporate registry or registered corporate service provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's confirmation letter or source-of-funds attestation for the subscribed share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter; apostille not imperative if the bank provides ISO or SWIFT correspondence, but consular legalization may be required for foreign banks in non-Apostille jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence must verify all SAS shareholders, directors, proposed UBOs, and authorized representatives against (i) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (iii) UN Security Council sanctions resolutions, (iv) French Direction Générale du Trésor financial sanctions and national list of frozen assets, (v) French les interdits de gérance (judicial ban on management), (vi) TRACFIN and ACPR AML/CFT management signals, and (vii) domestic and international PEP databases. For any match or PEP designator, a second review by the compliance director or external AML counsel is mandated. At least 48-month continuous transaction monitoring is expected once the entity is registered.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique Électronique de l'INPI (https://procedures.inpi.fr); also searched against the Registers of the Commercial Court via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) for existing company names, trademarks and established institutional signs.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS's corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin characters and generally in French, although foreign-language names are permitted. The name must not be contrary to French public order or good morals and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing business name, trademark, or an official statutory institution. If the corporate name is expressed in non-Latin script, a standardized transliteration into the Latin alphabet is mandatory; the official registration and all public notice filings are made only in the transliterated form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the INPI or the Commercial Registry, the applicant may: (1) file an administrative objection to the INPI Director General's office within 2 months of the rejection, using the e-recours system; (2) alternatively, submit a direct civil request to the competent Tribunal judiciaire of the registered office location; (3) before filing an appeal, an amended re-filing can be made via the Guichet Unique if the rejected name is corrected; (4) if rejection is based on a prior third-party right, actively obtain a waiver letter or non-opposition certificate from the prior rights holder and attach it to a new filing. Reservation extensions are not granted ex officio; a new application must be lodged within 30 days of the original reservation expiry, unless a pending appeal or a judicial order prevents refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if the SAS uses a registered domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) governed by Articles L123-11-1 and R123-166-1 of the French Commercial Code. A professional domiciliation must maintain a physical French address, assume a mailbox service, accept official service of documents, and provide regulatory access through a managed lease. For a 'pure equity holding' with no French employees, virtual offices are generally accepted provided the French domiciliation agent maintains clear records, the UBO and statutory books are accessible, and the entity does not create a false image of day-to-day management from France that would mislead third parties. Substance standards for French tax residence require actual decision-making and adequate supervision; if no economic substance exists, the enterprise may be exposed to anti-abuse challenges, but a simple holding SPV using a professional domiciliation service is an established practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-medium quantified risk: approximately 3–7% per annum for a passive holding company with a professional domiciliation provider in Paris; the probability increases to 15–20% if (i) a UBO is designated as PEP, (ii) a central bank review occurs, (iii) a judicial MCF (Commission des infractions fiscales) procedure is launched, or (iv) the company is flagged by TRACFIN for unusual cash flows. Unannounced inspections by judicial police, ACPR or DGFiP may occur under the legal access framework and are substantively more frequent for entities holding regulated subsidiaries, not for a pure SPV.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance: exhaustive availability search of the corporate name against the RNCS, Infogreffe, INPI trademarks and customary law conflicts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Infogreffe platform and agent (registered legal intermediary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff and market rate for paralegal search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a legally authorized legal announcements newspaper (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated tariff for JAL advertisements in the jurisdiction of the registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SAS bylaws (statuts) in French, including corporate governance, share transfer restrictions and deemed incorporation formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for specialist cross-border M&A counsel (€1,500–€2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and legalization / apostille of foreign corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, power of attorney, UBO ledger; estimated five original documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent consular authority / apostille office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for notary fees plus per-document consular or apostille fee (€25–€40 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing fee with the Commercial Court / Greffe du tribunal de commerce through the Guichet Unique (including issuance of the Kbis extract and a certificate of registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff under Article L123-7 II of the French Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration registration and formal incorporation of the beneficial ownership register (RBE) with the registrar using the mandatory AML/CFT formatting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed national e-filing fee for RBE declarations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional domiciliation arrangement for a passive holding company (12-month contract with a registered Paris domiciliation agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate (€20–€50 per month depending on mail handling and inspection supervision)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT enhanced due diligence: 24-month PEP, OFAC, EU consolidated list, UN and TRACFIN sanctions screening for the shareholder, UBOs, directors and authorized individuals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider / registered KYC vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per identity screening fee and subscription cost for the European sanction/PEP database

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion on civil and tax implications of the SAS incorporation, passive holding status, and verification of the foreign UBO's authentication chain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm / avocat specializing in corporate and international tax
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee for a concise opinion letter (€1,200–€2,500)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II: Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (formation and legal personality), L.123-1 et seq. (Registre National des Entreprises) and L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Code monétaire et financier Article L.561-45 (register of beneficial owners).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); local documentary control exercised by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the competent arrondissement.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Formulaire M0) filed electronically via the Guichet Unique, accompanied by signed statuts, capital blockage certificate, legal announcement proof, and identity documents, resulting in inscription at the RNE/RCS and issuance of the extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for an SAS (may be as low as EUR 1); the capital fixed in the statuts must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked funds account with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations before registration and are released only upon issuance of the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the draft Articles of Association be adopted in their entirety as the company's governing instrument. Resolved that the share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares, be subscribed and allotted to the subscriber(s) named in the subscription form. Resolved that the registered office be established at [address], as set out in Article 4 of the Articles. Resolved that [Name] be appointed President (Président) of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, with full power to represent the company toward third parties. Resolved that the President and any authorized agent be, jointly or severally, authorized to complete all filings and formalities necessary for company registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders, optionally assisted by a French legal practitioner; notarial authentication (acte notarié) required only for certain in-kind contributions, e.g. real property.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, stating corporate name, legal form (SAS), duration, registered office, corporate purpose limited to passive holding of subsidiary shares, share capital amount and class of shares, governance rules, powers of the President, and decision-making procedures. Each founder must sign every copy; if contributions in kind of real estate are made, the statuts must be notarized before filing.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts
Identity documentation of each founder (valid passport or national ID card)
Domiciliation agreement or title/lease evidencing the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies drafting defects, amend the statuts by a written supplementary resolution of the founders and re-execute; corrected versions are substituted in the filing package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital in a Blocked Funds Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked funds account in the name of the company in formation via a banking form; transfer all cash subscription proceeds by wire; instruct the bank to maintain the funds frozen until presentation of the Kbis extract. Obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds certifying the deposit and the blocked status.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application and KYC forms
Draft or executed statuts
Identity documents of signatories and beneficial owners
Proof of source of funds and AML declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the application under AML/KYC rules, provide supplementary bank statements and source-of-wealth explanations; if refusal persists, appoint a different credit institution or use Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and obtain a new capital blockage certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcements gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) authorized to operate in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the notice containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, and duration; submit the notice and pay the publication fee; collect the attestation de parution evidencing publication, which must be included in the incorporation dossier and remains valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Completed publication order form
Text of the legal notice
Copy of the draft statuts or a certificate of the founder confirming statutory particulars
Payment of the gazette fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette requires rectification, publish a corrective second notice and obtain an amended attestation de parution; if the original notice contains errors affecting third parties, a rectification notice must be published before filing or after registration, as appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which transmits the file to the RNE and the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 declaration on the official single window: enter company particulars and beneficial owner data, upload all annexes in PDF, pay the registration fee, and submit. The Guichet Unique issues the ackknowledgement of filing; the file is then examined by the registry for statutory conformity and criminal record checks of the President.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Formulaire M0 declaration
Executed statuts (one original or certified copy)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (blocked capital certificate)
Attestation de parution from the Journal d'Annonces Légales
Domiciliation certificate or lease for the registered office
Copy of identity documents of all founders and the President
Declaration of beneficial owners (formulaire bénéficiaires effectifs)
Sworn declaration of no criminal convictions (attestation de non-condamnation) for the President and, if applicable, other authorized managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry marks the file as incomplete or non-compliant, correct the deficiencies via the Guichet Unique within the statutory response delay and re-upload corrected documents; if the filing is declared irregular, submit an explanatory cover letter and, where lawful, request a judicial regularization order under Article L.210-7 of the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration, RNE Enrollment, and Issuance of the Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (local commercial registry) under the coordination of the Registre National des Entreprises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation, the registry enters the company in the RCS/RNE, assigns the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, and issues the extrait Kbis, which is the official proof of incorporation and legal personality of the SAS.
required_dossiers: No further dossiers: the Kbis is generated automatically from the validated M0 file
Third-party copies of the Kbis are ordered directly from the registry or online portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis extract contains erroneous information, file a written rectification request with the Greffe and the INPI; meanwhile request an attestation of registration in progress; any delay beyond the SLA should be escalated to the Greffe's supervisory authority for resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Bank Release of Capital, and Compliance Ancillaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The appointed President and founders; the Guichet Unique for declarations; the operational bank for fund release; the RNE/Greffe for annual filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Kbis to the bank to authorize release of the blocked funds; open the permanent corporate bank account; update the register of beneficial owners whenever BO data changes; complete any ancillary tax registration formalities (SIRET verification, VAT if applicable); keep the statutory records and prepare annual accounts for deposit with the Greffe within six months of year-end.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
Presidential powers certificate or board resolution appointing the President
Corporate bank account opening forms and AML declarations
Beneficial owner register updates, if any
Annual accounts (to be prepared and deposited later)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to release funds or open an account, provide the Kbis plus the President's proof of authority and escalate through the bank's internal complaint mechanism; if persistent, select another authorized bank; any rejection of RBE updates is cured by filing amended beneficial owner information via the Guichet Unique.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure equity holding SPV; no industrial licensing board competence is engaged. If the company later acquires operational assets, the residual competent authorities would be the DREETS (labor and company inspections) and the Préfecture through DREAL (environmental matters).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating permit required: the passive holding of subsidiary shares and receipt of corporate dividends (ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112) is exempt from French sectoral licensing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) under the Ministère de la Transition Écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-classified activity; no full EIA, no environmental authorization, and no IED permit required for the pure holding company.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for pure shareholding; if future occupied premises are operated, applicable thresholds under ICPE general provisions and local sanitary sewer/stormwater standards would apply; zero regulated wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the holding activity itself.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a passive holding SPV. If commercial premises are occupied, the following may apply: fire safety conformity attestation (ERP/IGH rules), electrical and structural safety certificates, waste collection contracts, and workplace health-and-safety compliance checks by DREETS.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online portal: impots.gouv.fr; local operational service for enterprises: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); central e-invoicing/e-reporting platform: Chorus Pro.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-established SAS, incorporation is completed through the Guichet unique (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), which triggers allocation of a SIREN/SIRET identification number by INSEE; the SIREN is the statutory corporate tax identification number, and the intra-Community VAT number is subsequently assigned by DGFiP. For a foreign entity not established in France, registration for French VAT requires a specific procedure: an EU-established taxable person must file Form 14264 (Cerfa n° 14264*02) with the competent SIE, provide proof of identity and foreign tax residence, and may use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for distance sales or pan-EU services; a non-EU established taxable person must additionally appoint a tax representative established in France and approved by DGFiP, file Form 14264, and submit the foreign registration certificate, constitutional documents, and certified powers of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is by statutory design subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level; it cannot elect pass-through treatment. No US-style check-the-box election exists under French domestic law. Elective mechanisms available to an SAS include: election into French tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under CGI Article 223 A if held at least 95% by a French parent; election for VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under CGI Article 256 C quater; and the automatic parent-subsidiary regime for 95% exempt intercompany dividends. Hybrid mismatch adjustments are mandatory and non-elective as transposed under EU ATAD, without taxpayers being able to choose fiscal transparency or opaque treatment against the French statutory classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_territ: French corporate income tax under the territoriality principle generally taxes only profits attributable to French activities or French real estate, except where the worldwide branch accounting regime has been elected.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_consolidation_and_anti_hybrid_notes: A parent entity, including a pure equity holding SPV, may elect French tax consolidation only if it is the head of a 95% group; where a foreign investor is the ultimate parent, specific anti-avoidance and arm's-length rules apply. France's hybrid mismatch regime is statute-based and cannot be overridden by check-the-box elections from another jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration turnover threshold applies to foreign taxable persons carrying on taxable supplies in France; registration is compulsory irrespective of turnover. For established micro-businesses, the French registration exemption and VAT franchise thresholds are EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services (2025 thresholds, subject to franchise en base conditions). The pre-2021 intra-EU distance-sales threshold for France was EUR 35,000 but has been repealed since 1 July 2021; distance sales are now taxable at destination and may be reported through the Union One-Stop-Shop without separate French VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing under the 2026-2027 reform. Large enterprises and intermediate-sized enterprises (ETI) must issue and receive e-invoices from 1 September 2026, while small and medium enterprises (PME/TPE) must comply from 1 September 2027. Suppliers must transmit standardized invoice data in compliance with Factur-X, UBL, or CII formats to Chorus Pro or a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP). B2B e-invoices require digital signature, certification, and near-real-time transmission for VAT audit. France does not currently operate a continuous transaction control model, but the reform is based on a clearance/e-reporting architecture requiring structured VAT data transmission to the fiscal authorities, with penalties for non-compliant issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under CGI Article 262-I, exports of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU are exempt and effectively zero-rated upon submission of proof of export; the seller must hold a valid export declaration (DAU) and cover transport documentation proving the goods left France or the EU within the statutory timeframes. Intra-Community supplies to a taxable person with a valid EU VAT number are exempt under CGI Article 262 ter, subject to the buyer communicating a valid VAT identification number and to the seller keeping an EC sales list. Services exported to non-EU B2B customers fall outside French VAT where the place of supply is deemed to be outside the EU under CGI Articles 259 and 259 A/B. For a pure equity holding SPV, dividends and share-sale proceeds are not export transactions for VAT purposes, but if the SPV incurs upstream or downstream supplies, the standard export substantiation rules apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / CAA Electronique) lodged through the French customs electronic clearance system
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (CMR, air waybill, rail consignment note, postal receipt)
Commercial invoice issued by the French supplier
Proof of payment and inward remittance certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds on French territory
Buyer's EU VAT identification number and EC sales list for exempt intra-Community supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is heavily audited by DGFiP and French customs. Where the exporter cannot produce satisfactory export documentation, the VAT originally zero-rated is clawed back, together with reversal of any input VAT credited to the exporter. Fraudulent claims may trigger penalties of 40% for bad-faith understatements and 80% for manoeuvres frauduleuses or abus de droit, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month and, under CGI Article 1741, criminal exposure for tax fraud, including imprisonment and fines. The supposed exporter may also be held jointly and severally liable for customs and VAT debts if transports or repatriation undertakings have been made without lawful substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) is the national central bank; the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) governs banking licensing and AML conduct; the Direction Générale du Trésor (DGT) within the Ministry for the Economy and Finance administers foreign-exchange regulatory policy and foreign-investment screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a full capital-account convertibility regime for the euro and all freely convertible currencies, in force since the 1990 'liberté des changes' liberalisation and consistent with EU capital movement rules. There is no exchange-control authorization, no prior licensing, and no profit-remittance approval required for an SAS to distribute dividends or repay shareholder advances, provided corporate law solvency tests (legal reserve of 5% of share capital, net assets above total capital) and the 30% withholding or treaty-reduced mechanism are respected. Practical constraints exist only for counterparties resident in FATF non-cooperative jurisdictions, triggering reinforced due diligence under Article L561-10 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF) and potential bank refusal of the MT103 clearing channel. Outbound direct investments from France are free except for the post-transaction statistical declarations to BdF and, where the SPV invests into a strategic-sector French target in the future, prior authorisation under French FDI screening rules (Decree 2019-1590).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable to a pure-equity holding SPV because the SAS has no trading or export turnover. As a general French rule, there is no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts: the surrender obligation was abolished in 1990 (CMF Art. L221-2). Exporters may keep non-euro proceeds indefinitely in approved foreign-currency accounts, provided the resident corporate entity reports each cross-border receipt and disbursement equal to or exceeding EUR 15,000 to Banque de France's balance-of-payments statistical department, either directly or through the banking intermediary, using the standard 'movements de fonds' declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) + Operational Current Account (compte courant)
Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) + Operational Current Account (compte courant)
Operational Current Account (compte courant); escrow only via subsidiary Crédit Mutuel CIC services
Operational Current Account (compte courant) with dedicated cross-border treasury desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary payment sub-accounts, Low to Medium as primary treasury rail. ACPR-licensed or EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Revolut Business may lawfully open payment accounts, execute SEPA and SWIFT transfers, and offer simple FX conversion under PSD2; however, EMIs cannot hold client funds beyond one business day, cannot grant credit or intraday liquidity, and are not permitted to act as custodian for the proceeds of capital subscriptions or dividend distributions where the SPV itself is the account counterparty. The legal boundary is set by CMF Articles L522-1 et seq. Consequently, a licensed credit institution remains mandatory for primary treasury purposes; an EMI may serve only as a disbursement sub-account for low-value operating expenses, and its use will nonetheless trigger enhanced due diligence under CMF Article D561-4-1.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Legal rule: remote video-identification is permitted under CMF Article R561-5-1 when using eIDAS-certified certificates and secure video verification, but the prevailing internal policy of the major tier-1 French banks requires at least one physical in-person KYC interview of a director or authorised legal representative, supported by original company sealing powers, RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract, and certified passport copies. For a non-resident UBO-owned SAS holding SPV, banks commonly mandate a hybrid opening: first remote pre-screening, then in-France physical interview at the commercial branch, unless the SPV is represented by a French avocat, notaire, or statutory auditor who has already carried out identity verification under CMF Article R561-5-5. Board approval must expressly name the signatories and the natural person responsible for AML reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-employee intermediate holding company with no administrative substance and entire benefit of participation exemption under Article 216 CGI
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified group organisational chart; lease or co-working agreement proving French physical presence; management agreement with fee schedule demonstrating arm's-length substance; audited financial statements of the SPV and the direct parent; notarial deed of incorporation and capital subscription statement; participation-exemption documentation (Articles 145 and 216 CGI) including holding-period evidence; board minutes attesting to quarterly strategic decisions taken in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the inbound equity injection, particularly if funds originate in an offshore trust or high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited investor financial statements for the last two years; original or certified bank statement of the investing shareholder covering 12 months of transaction history; sworn source-of-funds declaration (certificat de provenance des fonds) signed by the ultimate shareholder; trust deed and commercial rationale where a trust is involved; formal identification of the settlor and protectors; external FX sweeping records showing the euro conversion chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or legal representative appearing on a PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media watchlist
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declaration under CMF Article L561-10; live sanctions screening outputs from a reputable vendor (e.g., Refinitiv World-Check) covering OECD, EU, UN, and OFAC lists; qualified lawyer's legal opinion describing the lawfulness of the UBO's funds; bank references from the investee's existing banker; declaration of family and business relationships; commitment to ongoing transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate name containing 'SPV', 'Holding', or 'Gestion' with newly created status and high-speed capital inflows from non-EU parent
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed equity rationale memo (tax optimisation under the French parent-subsidiary regime, centralised treasury, IPO exit preparation); certificate of good standing from the relevant trade registry; full RBE certificate; letter from the French statutory auditor confirming no irregularity; verified track record of the parent's own banking relationship; projection of the SPV's balance sheet and cash flows showing passive holding activity and no trading risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: for intra-EEA contributions use SEPA Credit Transfer; for non-EEA and non-euro injections use SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary account title exactly matching the SAS registered name and RIB, and with field 72 completed with the purpose descriptor 'Apport en capital – Souscription d'actions' and the French balance-of-payments statistical code 22000 ('Direct investment – Equity capital'). The receiving bank is legally obliged to report to Banque de France any cross-border movement of EUR 15,000 or above (or aggregated daily flows exceeding that threshold) under the balance-of-payments declaration regime; the SPV must simultaneously file a notarial capital subscription statement and update the KRS/RBE within one month. For inbound injections over EUR 150,000, banks will additionally require written confirmation of the corporate interest, the passport of the ultimate investor, and an opinion of counsel on the tax classification (equity vs debt) to prevent disguised financing. Verification is completed by cross-matching three elements: the SWIFT GPI tracking receipt, the MT103 value-date confirmation, and the notary's certificate confirming completion of the capital increase.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer for euro disbursements to EEA beneficiaries, including instant SEPA Credit Transfer for amounts up to EUR 100,000 per transaction; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA or non-euro payments, with MT202/MT202COV used when the SPV clears through a correspondent bank to confer transparency on the beneficiary; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710, UCP600 rules) where the equity holding finances an underlying trading subsidiary that requires bank-confirmed settlement; (4) SEPA Direct Debit or TIPI filings for statutory payments to the French tax authority (DGFiP). Outbound dividend distributions or shareholder loan repayments must carry the tax reference (form 2561 or treaty certificate) and the payment code in the instruction message, and the SPV must maintain a full format log to evidence the economic rationale under transfer-pricing and anti-abuse documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (marché de change à terme) up to 18 months on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/JPY, traded OTC with a licensed French bank under a signed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or French FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) Master Agreement.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for restricted or non-deliverable currencies such as offshore CNY (EUR/CNH) or RUB, used only when the SPV receives economic exposure from a foreign subsidiary and cannot settle in that currency onshore.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (XCCY) for the re-denomination of intra-group shareholder loans from EUR to USD, including fixed-rate to floating-rate legs where appropriate.
FX Swap (swap de change) for temporary liquidity bridging before a capital increase is completed, with maturity not exceeding 90 days to avoid reclassification as a financial transaction.

Vanilla European FX Options (call/put) under the same ISDA/FBF frame, purchased or sold only when the SPV can evidence a real pre-existing exposure through audited subsidiary dividend forecasts or acquisition commitments; all trades are subject to EMIR transaction reporting, and clearing thresholds are assessed annually.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualifying small company may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory ownership, turnover, paid-in-capital and other conditions. Qualifying dividends received from subsidiaries may benefit from the participation exemption, generally excluding 95% of the dividend from the French corporate income tax base, leaving a 5% taxable share. The participation exemption generally requires at least 5% ownership and a two-year holding commitment. French tax losses are generally carried forward without a general time limit, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding year and capped at EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, filed with Forms 2058-A-SD through 2059-G-SD and applicable annexes through the French tax administration's EDI-TDFC electronic filing channel or an authorized filing intermediary.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate income tax instalments are generally paid four times per year, with the final balance paid through Form 2572-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the normal deadline is the second business day following 1 May of the following year. Electronic filing and payment are mandatory for companies subject to corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, registered office, French tax identification number, fiscal year dates, tax-consolidation status, and applicable corporate income tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the French SAS as the taxable entity even where all shareholders are non-resident. State the foreign parent only in the ownership, related-party or tax-consolidation sections where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or loss calculated from the statutory accounts after French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not report the worldwide income of a non-resident shareholder. Report only the French SAS's taxable result and French-law adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2058-A-SD, accounting result to taxable result reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the accounting profit or loss with the French tax result, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, provisions, participation-exemption adjustments and foreign-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude shareholder-level income and expenses. Dividends qualifying for the participation exemption require the statutory exempt-income treatment and add-back of the corresponding 5% share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report current-year and prior-year tax losses, utilized amounts, remaining carryforwards and any carryback claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses belong to the French SAS and cannot be transferred to a foreign shareholder except under an applicable French tax-consolidation or statutory reorganization regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2058-C-SD, taxable income and corporate income tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after loss utilization and determine the corporate income tax liability, including applicable rate adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary 25% rate unless the SAS independently satisfies the conditions for a reduced rate or other statutory relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose qualifying participations, ownership percentages, acquisition dates, subsidiary identities and relevant dividend information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include foreign subsidiaries and parent-related holdings where the form requires them. Maintain evidence of ownership, holding period, beneficial ownership and dividend entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2066-SD, foreign tax credits and foreign-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying foreign-source income and foreign withholding taxes for which a French credit or treaty mechanism is claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS may claim relief only to the extent permitted by French law and the relevant treaty. Attach or retain foreign withholding certificates and treaty support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay the applicable quarterly corporate income tax instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not file this form; the French SAS remains responsible for its own instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the final corporate income tax liability, credit instalments already paid and pay the balance or request a refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment reference and French tax account are matched to the SAS's SIREN and tax identification number.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% for fraudulent maneuvers, abuse of law or concealed activity. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and exceptions. Material inaccuracies may trigger additional penalties, loss of tax benefits and criminal referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2067-SD for deductible expenses paid to related or specified recipients, Form 2257-SD for the annual transfer-pricing statement where applicable, and Form 2746-SD for certain real-estate wealth-tax reporting obligations where applicable; filing is through EDI-TDFC or the relevant French electronic tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, where statutory thresholds or transaction categories apply.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed with the corporate income tax return or by the applicable annual deadline prescribed for the relevant form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report specified deductible expenses, including certain payments to related parties or recipients in low-tax jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include payments to foreign group companies when the statutory disclosure criteria are met, regardless of the recipient's residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the nature, amounts and counterparties of material controlled transactions and the existence of transfer-pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign parent, subsidiary, financing, royalty, service and cost-sharing transactions using consistent legal-entity names and tax residence codes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transmit the return and annexes in the required electronic format and retain the filing acknowledgment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder or director cannot replace the French SAS's filing obligation. Use a French tax representative or authorized intermediary where operationally necessary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file required transfer-pricing or related-party disclosures may result in specific administrative fines, tax reassessment, denial of deductions, transfer-pricing adjustments, late-payment interest and enhanced penalties for intentional conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on French-source dividends paid to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, applicable tax treaties and anti-abuse rules. Qualifying EU or EEA corporate shareholders may obtain an exemption where statutory ownership, subject-to-tax, holding-period and anti-abuse requirements are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the beneficial owner and verify treaty eligibility, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements, minimum ownership thresholds and holding periods. Apply the reduced treaty rate only where French procedural requirements are met; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund through the French tax administration. Maintain the dividend resolution, shareholder register, ownership evidence, tax residence certificate, treaty analysis, payment records and beneficial-owner representation. Treaty relief is unavailable where the recipient is a conduit, lacks beneficial ownership or the arrangement is abusive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding rate of 25%, subject to treaty reductions commonly ranging from 0% to 10% and to EU directive relief where applicable. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, subject to statutory exceptions, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, for which a 75% rate may apply. Treaties commonly allocate interest taxing rights exclusively or primarily to the residence state, subject to beneficial ownership, anti-abuse and special-interest provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million of annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets, or membership in or control of an enterprise meeting the statutory threshold, generally triggers full French transfer-pricing documentation obligations, including a Local File and Master File. A separate annual transfer-pricing statement may apply from EUR 50 million of annual turnover or gross assets or equivalent group-status conditions. Material controlled transactions must be documented even below these thresholds under the arm's-length principle.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single comprehensive ESR regime equivalent to certain offshore substance regimes. Substance is nevertheless assessed through the general anti-abuse rule, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse standards, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, interest-limitation rules, transfer-pricing rules, anti-hybrid rules and the abuse-of-law doctrine. A pure equity holding SAS should maintain French decision-making, appropriate directors, documented board deliberations, a French registered office, accounting and tax records, bank-account controls, evidence of investment monitoring and commercially credible functions. A conduit, nominee arrangement or entity lacking genuine control over dividends, financing or investments may lose treaty and participation-exemption benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing dividends, related-party income, beneficial ownership, taxable gains or deductible-expense limitations; submitting knowingly false accounts or tax returns; or fabricating supporting documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax reassessment, 40% or 80% penalties depending on intent and conduct, late-payment interest, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions. Ordinary tax fraud may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated circumstances may increase exposure to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, with higher amounts possible under applicable provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil damages and personal tax liability where their fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct makes collection impossible under Article L.267 of the French Tax Procedures Code. Court-ordered management bans may apply. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require a specific judicial or enforcement basis; imprisonment is possible for criminal tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of law, treaty abuse and artificial holding structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the SAS solely to obtain treaty-reduced withholding, dividend exemption or another tax advantage without genuine investment, governance, financing or commercial rationale; routing income to a non-beneficial owner or conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic relief, reassessment of withholding tax and corporate income tax, abuse-of-law penalties generally up to 80% or 40% depending on the taxpayer's role and circumstances, and late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for intentional misconduct, criminal exposure where false documents or fraud are involved, management bans and personal tax recovery actions in cases of fraudulent or seriously negligent management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length financing, management fees, guarantees, royalties or service charges to shift profits from or into France without contemporaneous functional analysis and supporting evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment of taxable income, possible secondary adjustment or withholding-tax consequences, denial of deductions, documentation penalties, 40% or 80% penalties where intentional or abusive, and late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for knowingly approving sham or unsupported transactions, false accounting or asset diversion. Criminal liability depends on proof of fraud, forgery, misuse of corporate assets or other statutory offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file, pay or maintain accounting records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late corporate income tax filing, unpaid instalments, failure to electronically file, omission of mandatory annexes, incomplete books or inability to substantiate transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% late-filing surcharge, late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, additional penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct, and possible rejection of unsupported deductions or estimated assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS is primarily liable. Directors may become personally liable under statutory tax-recovery rules where their serious negligence or fraudulent management prevents collection and may also incur civil liability to the company or creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without distributable profits, distributing fictitious dividends, making repayments disguised as dividends, or bypassing required shareholder approval and statutory reserve rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, director liability, possible criminal sanctions for fictitious dividends or misuse of corporate assets, tax reassessment and withholding-tax exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize unlawful distributions may be jointly liable for restitution and damages and may face criminal sanctions, management bans and asset-seizure measures where applicable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering, sanctions and beneficial-owner violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the holding company to layer illicit funds, conceal the ultimate beneficial owner, process sanctioned-party payments, or make unexplained cross-border transfers through bank or SWIFT channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Account freezes, confiscation, administrative or criminal penalties, reporting obligations, regulatory enforcement and, for money laundering, imprisonment and substantial fines that may be increased by statutory aggravating factors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be prosecuted personally for money laundering, sanctions evasion or concealment, with imprisonment, fines, confiscation, professional or management bans and judicial travel restrictions where ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting, misuse of corporate assets and document fabrication
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording sham loans, circular payments, fictitious services, concealed related-party transactions or false board and shareholder documents to support repatriation or tax positions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil restitution, accounting and corporate criminal sanctions, tax reassessment, penalties, confiscation and potential imprisonment depending on the offense and intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers and de facto managers may be personally liable for restitution, creditor losses, criminal fines, imprisonment, management bans and confiscation of assets connected with the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to preserve economic substance and corporate governance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SAS solely as a nominee or mailbox entity, allowing a foreign parent to make all decisions without documented French governance, or failing to maintain records evidencing investment-management functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of treaty and participation-exemption positions, withholding-tax reassessment, denial of deductions, transfer-pricing adjustments, abuse-of-law penalties and reputational or banking consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for breach of management duties and personal exposure where the structure is used fraudulently. Imprisonment or travel bans require proof of a separate criminal offense and judicial action; they are not automatic consequences of insufficient substance alone.
